Systems built

From single tasks to systems that run on their own

Part of the work went into building systems in which AI agents do work that would not otherwise be done: reading the research and the news every day, rebuilding historical data series, collecting evidence across dozens of countries, answering questions over an economic model. These systems are where most of the new tasks in the log come from. Their value depends on whether their output can be trusted, so each is built around feedback loops that check the agents’ work.

The systems

System

Data-extraction pipeline

Agents rebuild historical time series from archived web pages and documents, one year per agent, with every value quoted from its source and checked by an independent agent on a different model. Two pilots ran in September; the team approved scaling it up, one country first. Since November it runs on its own agent loop, ready for a wider scope.

System

News radar for the team

An unattended radar that reads public company reporting and the trade press every day, groups coverage into evidence-tiered stories and keeps them in a structured library. A topic expert reviews items through simple forms, and that feedback goes back into the system. Live since late October.

System

Agentic policy simulator

A chat interface over an existing economic model. Questions go to the deterministic model, which produces every figure; the language model only words the answer, and checks reject any figure the model did not produce. Built in June and July 2026.

System

Research radar

Two daily, unattended reviews of new work on AI in the social sciences and in AI engineering. Each development is verified, scored, de-duplicated and archived. Its library feeds the literature behind this report and the method used in the other systems.

Method

Evidence log and playbook

The log behind this site: one validated entry per task, built weekly from the agent’s usage data and my judgements. It also collects each project’s weekly lessons on building with agents into a knowledge base and a public playbook of rules for new projects.

Method

Web search agents for empirical analysis

In the MVNO wholesale access study, agents searched the web to build the treatment variable: MVNO access regulation, by type, for 30 European countries. They also found the market share of MVNOs across Europe. That meant going through hundreds of web pages from different countries, in different languages: work a person could do in principle, but that would not realistically have been done by hand.

How the systems are made trustworthy

Trust comes from feedback loops, not from the model. The method is feedback loop engineering (D. Demmel): agents check their own work against real evidence, independent readers check it again, and every human correction becomes a rule or a check for the next run.

What the projects have taught so far is written down as they go. counted from the files

16

weekly handovers from projects on what they learned about building with agents

18

patterns reached independently in two or more projects

17 + 15

core and candidate rules in the playbook for new projects

Some of the lessons that recur:

  • Judgement to the model, guarantees to code. Anything that must always hold is enforced by a script the agent cannot change, never by an instruction.
  • Check what is missing, not only what was recorded. Two readers can agree perfectly on a dataset that is missing a whole category. A domain expert found one such gap in a few minutes; sensors for omissions followed.
  • A failure must never look like an empty result. An aborted step, a stale input or a cut-off file must stop the run loudly.
  • Count with scripts, not memory. Every figure in a report comes from a command.
